messages:
marta: FYI Orchid reported a sudden throughput drop for short requests after yesterday's kernel-selector push. They see ~25% lower tokens/s for batch sizes 1-4, seq <= 64. Can someone run a quick microbench and flamegraph?

kai: on it. which model/variant and can you paste an example request id?

marta: model=redwood-3b-q4, variant=fast-kernel, request id: 0x9af2b7. workload: small batched chat (batch 1-4), seq 16 typical. KV cache enabled. customer noticed it around 2026-03-14 23:10 UTC right after rollout.

alex: pinging @irene for profiling. also check if kernel-selector fell back to slower path for short seqs.

irene: I'll spin up a staging run. running:
```
bench_runner --model redwood-3b-q4 --variant fast-kernel --batches 1,2,4 --seq 16 --iters 500 --profile flame --output /tmp/orchid-1850001234
```
Uploading flamegraphs to https://dash.redwood.internal/perf/orchid/1850001234 when done.

perf-bot: queued bench job (id: bench-1850001234-1). ETA ~7m.

kai: while that's running, can someone share the deployment diff? maybe a config flag changed for small-seq kernel choice.

marta: here's the rollout PR: https://git.internal/redwood/serving/pulls/8421 — main change was kernel_selector: prefer_latency_over_throughput = true for seq <= 64.

samir: thanks. adding a canary-revert plan in case. I've created a rollback playbook: /runbooks/deploys/revert-kernel-selector.md — but let's confirm perf impact first.

irene: bench done. quick numbers:
```
batch 1: baseline (pre-rollout) 120 tok/s -> current 88 tok/s (-26%)
batch 2: 210 -> 160 (-24%)
batch 4: 360 -> 280 (-22%)
```
Flamegraph shows hot loops in attention kernel path A vs B — selector now picks A for short seq. Uploading artifacts.

alex: if kernel A is more latency-optimized but has worse throughput for many small batches, that's a regression in our throughput SLOs. Could be due to removed vectorization fallback.

kai: can we force selector to prefer path B for seq<=64 as a quick canary?

irene: yes, test command to simulate:
```
echo "force_selector=pathB" > /etc/redwood/selector_override && systemctl restart redwood-serving
```
I pushed a canary override on staging and reran bench: batch1 118 tok/s, batch2 208, batch4 355 — matches baseline.

marta: great. let's schedule a minimal rollback for the flag in prod and coordinate CS. @samir can you own the rollout?

samir: I can do the flag revert in prod during the 10m maintenance window in 30m. I'll follow runbook and announce to customer.

deploy-bot: prod-flag-revert job scheduled by samir for 2026-03-15T14:40:00Z.

alex: follow-up items: 1) revert short-seq preference until we have perf tests in CI, 2) add short-seq throughput benchmarks to pre-merge, 3) write a selector unit test to assert throughput delta <10%.

marta: agreed. I'll file the ticket and assign owners. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: artifacts uploaded: https://dash.redwood.internal/perf/orchid/1850001234/artifacts.zip

irene: capturing notes in the incident doc: /incidents/2026-03-15-orchid-kselector.md — will add flamegraphs and commands.

marta: closing the slack thread once prod revert is confirmed.

samir: prod revert completed, customer confirmed throughput back to baseline. closing. :white_check_mark:
